description: Use this when asked to check an AI agent or MCP server: does it work, is it reachable, is its card valid ("check this agent", "is this MCP server up?"). Pass just its `url`. Returns READY / FIXES_NEEDED / NO_AGENT_CARD / UNREACHABLE with fixes and a receipt. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

data_classification.description: PUBLIC (default) or NON_PERSONAL_PUBLIC. Never send personal data.

declared_identity.description: Optional: the name the agent claims.

expected_endpoint.description: Optional: the endpoint you expect; a different primary endpoint is reported as ENDPOINT_DRIFT.

intended_task.description: VERIFY_BEFORE_CALL: what you intend to delegate.

metadata.description: Alternative to url: the agent card or MCP/OpenAPI document itself.

mode.description: CONFORMANCE (default) checks the interface; VERIFY_BEFORE_CALL returns task-specific evidence about `target` for `intended_task`.

protocol.description: Counterparty protocol. Inferred from metadata when omitted, otherwise MCP.

source_url.description: Optional: where `metadata` was published, used only to resolve relative endpoints. Never fetched.

target.description: VERIFY_BEFORE_CALL: the counterparty URL or reference.

url.description: Public https link to an agent, its A2A agent card, MCP server description or OpenAPI document. GAIP fetches, validates and reach-tests it. Use instead of metadata.

name: check_agent_conformance
title: Check an AI agent or MCP server

description: Use this before your agent fetches a page ("may my agent fetch this?"). Pass the `url` and your `agent` token. Reads robots.txt (RFC 9309), AI-preference lines, RSL, tdmrep.json and llms.txt; returns ALLOWED, DISALLOWED, NO_RULE or UNKNOWN, the rule quoted, the time and a signature. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

agent.description: Your agent's user-agent token as robots.txt names it, e.g. GPTBot or ClaudeBot (a full User-Agent string also works). Default * (any crawler without its own rules).

url.description: The public https URL your agent wants to fetch.

user_agent.description: Alternative to agent: your agent's full User-Agent string.

name: gaip_check_permission
title: May my agent fetch this?

description: Use this when asked what changed between two versions of an agent card, MCP server description or OpenAPI document ("did this API break?"). Pass `prior` and `current`. Returns each change as BREAKING / NON_BREAKING / INFO with migration notes and a receipt. Free, no account; records a GAIP receipt only. Inputs must be public and non-personal.

continuity_handle.description: Optional: the continuity_handle from an earlier GAIP result; links this call to your earlier ones.

counterparty_id.description: Name or URL of the agent/service. Optional.

current.description: The later version, same kind as `prior`.

data_classification.description: PUBLIC (default) or NON_PERSONAL_PUBLIC. Never send personal data.

episode_id.description: Optional: your own id to group related calls.

independent_operator_id.description: Optional: your operator id (recorded as a claim, not verified).

prior.description: The earlier version: agent card, MCP server description, OpenAPI document or snapshot.

protocol.description: Counterparty protocol. Inferred from metadata when omitted, otherwise MCP.

synthetic.description: Optional: true marks a test call.

task_class.description: Optional: short name of the task, e.g. weather_forecast.

name: gaip_compare_supplier_snapshots
title: What changed between two versions

description: Use this when an agent, MCP or API call failed ("why did my call fail?", "what does this 429 mean?"). Pass the `failure` ({code, detail}) or the raw error text. Returns the likely cause, when and how to retry, fix steps and a receipt. GAIP touches no other system. Free, no account; records a GAIP receipt only. Inputs must be public and non-personal.

continuity_handle.description: Optional: the continuity_handle from an earlier GAIP result; links this call to your earlier ones.

counterparty_id.description: Name or URL of the agent/service. Optional.

data_classification.description: PUBLIC (default) or NON_PERSONAL_PUBLIC. Never send personal data.

episode_id.description: Optional: your own id to group related calls.

failure.description: The failure: {code, detail?, http_status?}, e.g. {"code": 429, "detail": "Too Many Requests; Retry-After: 20"}.

independent_operator_id.description: Optional: your operator id (recorded as a claim, not verified).

protocol.description: Counterparty protocol. Inferred from metadata when omitted, otherwise MCP.

synthetic.description: Optional: true marks a test call.

task_class.description: Optional: short name of the task, e.g. weather_forecast.

name: gaip_diagnose_integration_failure
title: Why did my agent call fail?

description: Use this when asked which MCP servers or agents changed recently ("what changed this week?"). Optional `since` (RFC 3339), `target_id`, `limit` (max 100). Returns the Observatory's hash-chained log of manifest changes: before/after hashes, neutral facts, receipts. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.
name: gaip_manifest_changes
title: What changed recently (manifest log)

description: Use this to save a dated record of what a public MCP server or A2A agent card declares now. Pass its `url`. GAIP reads it once (robots.txt respected, never tools/call), re-reads it daily and returns the capture id, time and SHA-256 hashes. Not an assessment. Free, no account; records a GAIP receipt only. Inputs must be public and non-personal.

examples.url: <public https URL of the MCP endpoint or A2A agent card to save>

protocol.description: Optional; inferred from the URL (a /.well-known/agent-card.json path is A2A).

url.description: Public https URL of the MCP endpoint or the A2A agent card.

name: gaip_observatory_capture
title: Save an agent's declarations now

description: Use this when asked about an MCP server's or agent's history ("has this server changed?", "was it up last week?"). Pass its `url` or `name`. Returns dated facts the Agent Observatory observed: status history, manifest hash, conformance codes, change log. Not an assessment. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

name.description: Optional: server or agent name to search for.

url.description: Public URL of the MCP server or agent to look up.

name: gaip_observatory_lookup
title: Look up an MCP server's or agent's history

description: Use this when a supplier agent or API you depend on started failing ("did something change on their side?"). Pass its `supplier_url` and the `failure`. Returns the diagnosis plus changes GAIP observed around then (correlated in time, not causation), with receipts. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

card.description: Optional supplier card / server description you integrated against.

data_classification.description: PUBLIC (default) or NON_PERSONAL_PUBLIC. Never send personal data.

failure_started_at.description: Optional: RFC 3339 time the failures started.

lookback_days.description: Optional: days of GAIP observations to look back over.

protocol.description: Omit to infer it from card, transport or the supplier URL path (else UNKNOWN).

supplier_url.description: Public https URL of the supplier's agent card, MCP server or API.

task_class.description: Optional: short name of the task, e.g. weather_forecast.

transport.description: Optional transport you used (e.g. streamable-http, sse, GRPC).

name: gaip_supplier_reliability
title: Why is my supplier failing?

description: Use this before connecting to an MCP server: did its tools change since your `since` date? Pass its `url`, optionally your tools/list `tools` or a digest. Returns dates, change classes, stored hashes and whether yours match the latest GAIP observed. Facts, not a verdict. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

since.description: Your approval date (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD): changes recorded since then.

tool_digests.description: Per-tool digests in the DRAFT MCP SEP-2636 form (may change).

tools.description: The `tools` array from your own tools/list; GAIP hashes it and compares.

tools_digest.description: A SHA-256 (64 hex) of the tool list you approved, as GAIP reported it.

url.description: The MCP endpoint (or A2A agent card) URL, exactly as you connect to it.

name: gaip_tools_changed_since
title: Has this MCP server changed?

description: Use this when asked what changed on a watched agent or service. Pass your `continuity_handle` and optionally a `watch_id`. Returns recent change events: verdict before and after, a change summary, the receipt and webhook delivery status. Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

continuity_handle.description: The continuity_handle from an earlier GAIP result; proves you own these watches.

name: gaip_watch_events
title: Read watch change events

description: Use this when asked which agents or services you are watching. Pass your `continuity_handle`. Returns each watch's kind, target, last verdict, last and next check and webhook endpoint (never the secret). Free, read-only, no account; inputs must be public and non-personal.

continuity_handle.description: The continuity_handle from an earlier GAIP result; proves you own these watches.

name: gaip_watch_list
title: List my watches

description: Use this when asked to keep an eye on an agent or MCP server ("tell me if it changes or goes down"). Pass the `continuity_handle` from any GAIP result, `kind` and `target_url`. GAIP re-checks every 24 hours (3 free watches), receipts each change and can call your webhook. Free, no account; records a GAIP receipt only. Inputs must be public and non-personal.

continuity_handle.description: The continuity_handle from an earlier GAIP result; proves you own these watches.

data_classification.description: PUBLIC (default) or NON_PERSONAL_PUBLIC. Never send personal data.

interval_hours.description: Hours between checks: 24 minimum on the free tier; 1 for DELIVERY_SLA.

kind.description: AGENT_READINESS (agent URL), SUPPLIER_CARD (published card), DELIVERY_TERMS (terms_id) or DELIVERY_SLA (terms_id plus sla terms).

sla.description: DELIVERY_SLA only: service-level terms checked on every observation, any of min_uptime_pct, max_latency_ms, required_fields (JSON key paths), freshness_field + max_age_seconds; optional uptime_window_hours, min_observations. Results go only to you.

target_url.description: Public https URL (AGENT_READINESS, SUPPLIER_CARD). No query string.

terms_id.description: DELIVERY_TERMS or DELIVERY_SLA: terms_id from witness_register_terms.

webhook_url.description: Optional: your own public https endpoint for signed change events.

name: gaip_watch_register
title: Watch an agent or MCP server for changes

description: Use this when asked to stop watching an agent or service. Pass your `continuity_handle` and the `watch_id`. Its stored events are deleted; retained receipts stay verifiable. Free, no account; records a GAIP receipt only. Inputs must be public and non-personal.

continuity_handle.description: The continuity_handle from an earlier GAIP result; proves you own these watches.

name: gaip_watch_remove
title: Remove a watch
